title: Google Cloud Launches AI-powered Agents to Simplify Database Lifecycle Management
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/google-database-operation-agents/en/headerimage/google-database-operations-agents-1787842474177.jpeg"/><p>Google Cloud has introduced AI-powered Database Operations Agents, featuring an Onboarding Agent that streamlines database setup and an Observability Agent that helps automate troubleshooting, performance optimization, and tuning. Integrated with Gemini Cloud Assist, these agents support multiple database services, including AlloyDB, Bigtable, and Spanner.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Cloudflare Wallets Arrives Late to x402, and the Spending Controls Stop at the Payment
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/agent-payment-rails-x402/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787649155466.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare announced Wallets, giving agents a stablecoin balance and spending controls, though only handle claiming is live and squatting complaints have already surfaced. Payments run on x402, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. The controls bound single payments, not sequences, leaving composition to the application above.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Presentation: Can Claude Fix Itself? Using LLMs for Incident Response
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/claude-sre-incidents/en/mediumimage/alex-palcuie-medium-1786539336984.jpg"/><p>Anthropic reliability engineer Alex Palcuie shares practical lessons on using LLMs for real-world incident response. He explains where AI acts as a superhuman for observing logs and traces, why it still struggles with causation versus correlation during root-cause analysis, and how engineering leaders can integrate AI into on-call workflows without eroding human expertise.</p> <i>By Alex Palcuie</i>

title: Diagrid Catalyst 2.0 Adds Durable and Verifiable Execution for AI Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/diagrid-catalyst-ai-agents/en/headerimage/header-1787430272425.jpeg"/><p>Diagrid Catalyst 2.0 applies Dapr-based recovery, signed workflow history and execution attestation across several agent frameworks. Architects should compare it with framework-native durability and established workflow engines, while evaluating benchmark evidence and operational trade-offs.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Presentation: Continuous Delivery for Foundational Platforms
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/cd-reliability-innovation/en/mediumimage/ian-nowland-medium-1787217621961.jpg"/><p>Ian Nowland discusses why conventional CI/CD practices break down for stateful, core infrastructure. Drawing from his leadership at AWS and Datadog, he shares actionable techniques for safe progressive deployments, synthetic testing in production, and mitigating blast radius in complex software platforms.</p> <i>By Ian Nowland</i>

title: BMC Vulnerabilities Put Thousands of Servers at Risk of Hardware-Level Compromise
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/bmc-vulnerabilities/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787152274946.jpg"/><p>Security researchers are warning that thousands of enterprise servers could be exposed to compromise through vulnerabilities in their Baseboard Management Controllers (BMCs) - specialized processors embedded in server motherboards that provide administrators with remote, out-of-band control.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Cursor Releases Origin as an Agent-Native Alternative to GitHub
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/cursor-origin-alternative-github/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787588546610.jpg"/><p>AI coding agent Cursor has launched Origin, a git based code hosting platform embedded inside its AI-powered editor, positioning it as an alternative to GitHub for teams that already work in Cursor. Origin is rolling out in early beta on Pro, Teams and Enterprise plans, and lives inside a new Codebase tab within the Cursor application.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Beyond Embedded: How DuckDB v2.0 Shifts Architecture toward Distributed Network Capabilities
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>DuckDB Labs has previewed DuckDB v2.0, codenamed "Cyanoptera." This release includes over 10000 commits and introduces a client/server mode, enabling network connections. Improvements also encompass extension portability, advanced data types, and a new parser. Performance enhancements include asynchronous I/O and storage optimisations. General availability is expected in fall 2026.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Article: Rightsizing Platform Engineering: Building the Platform Your Organization Actually Needs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/rightsizing-platform-engineering/en/smallimage/rightsizing-platform-engineering-thumbnail-1787296955801.jpg"/><p>Shift-left and DevOps have impacted how we flow changes from inception to production, but at the cost of increased cognitive load and duplication of effort across testing, security, and maintenance. This article explores the real-world challenges of rightsizing developer platforms and finding a cultural match for engineering teams who use them to reduce cognitive load and deliver change faster.</p> <i>By John Keates</i>

title: Presentation: Prompt to Prod: Engineering an Autonomous SDLC at Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/autonomous-ai-software-development-roblox/en/mediumimage/andrew-swerdlow-medium-1787218240356.jpg"/><p>Andrew Swerdlow shares how Roblox scales autonomous software development from prompt to production. He discusses building robust security sandboxes, extracting institutional knowledge via code review exemplars, updating engineering infrastructure, and redefining productivity metrics around feature velocity and long-running AI turns to achieve trusted, automated deployment at scale.</p> <i>By Andrew Swerdlow</i>

title: OVHcloud Raises Prices as AI Memory Demand Reprices Non-AI Infrastructure
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/ovhcloud-memory-price-rise/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787136997592.jpg"/><p>OVHcloud will raise prices from September, with 2026-edition gaming servers up 87 percent and other recent servers 40 to 59 percent. Founder Octave Klaba says memory cost six times more in June than a year earlier, as RAM suppliers shifted capacity toward high-bandwidth memory for AI. AWS, buying years ahead, has repriced one reserved GPU product.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: DRAM Controller Register Manipulation Breaks CPU Memory Isolation
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Security researcher Christopher Domas developed skitter-creek-bath-salts, an open-source hardware security tool that disrupts CPU privilege boundaries by manipulating memory controller translation registers. This allows unprivileged software to access protected memory regions, revealing a vulnerability in modern processor architectures that could affect cloud and confidential computing security.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Presentation: SafeChat: Building AI-Powered Safety Systems at Scale in a Real-Time Marketplace
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/doordash-llm-ai-moderation-platform/en/mediumimage/bruna-pereira-medium-1786539036040.jpeg"/><p>Bruna Pereira explains how DoorDash built a content-agnostic AI moderation platform. She covers replacing costly LLM-only pipelines with a hybrid pattern: using fast internal models to filter obvious cases, LLM multi-axis scoring for nuanced decisions, and no-code workflows with backtesting. Discover how this architectural pattern cut safety incidents while scaling to millions of daily messages.</p> <i>By Bruna Pereira</i>

title: AI Code Review at Scale: LinkedIn's Multi-Agent Approach
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/linkedin-ai-code-review/en/headerimage/linkedin-code-review-1787387463447.jpeg"/><p>At LinkedIn's scale, relying solely on human reviewers or simply putting an off-the-shelf AI reviewer in front of GitHub is not an effective way to manage PRs. To address this, LinkedIn engineers built a multi-agent AI code review platform that understands the organization's coding context, treats code review as production infrastructure, and minimizes hallucinations and low-signal feedback.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Cloudflare Turns Engineering Standards into an AI-Enforced Control System
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/cloudflare-ai-enforcement/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1786356220839.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has recently detailed how it is using AI to transform internal engineering standards from passive documentation into an actively enforced control system across the software development lifecycle.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>
